The frozen COMMITMENT_HEADER in src/swarm/evals/g13_sealed_reference.py named the very words it promised to exclude: 'no reference answer, no grader fixture, no rubric, no answer digest'. The rendered file therefore contained the substring grader and the assertion failed on every run, including at the exact tips 6467552f86e40964e5bd26d85e3b3a74d03aa059 and f7800332594d67c8b872b3597abd59f35987a2a0.

No task-pool assertion was deleted, skipped, xfailed or loosened.

independence_design.axis_one: g13-independence-checker-v2, fail-closed on four intra-holdout and four cross-partition id, payload-digest, prompt-digest and normalised-template invariants
independence_design.axis_two: g13-semantic-group-axis-v1, fail-closed on semantic archetype depth per required cell
independence_design.scenario_noun_discipline: the same fifteen scenario nouns are used in every one of the sixteen cells, and each noun occurs exactly twice in a record: once as the scenario field and once inside the instruction carrier. A scenario noun never appears in an item, a constraint, a distractor, a question, a signature or an output contract. The scenario therefore carries no archetype information at all, which is what makes it safe to erase.
independence_design.planning_dependency_shape: a spine of exactly depth-many edges over the first depth plus one steps, plus a fan-out of single edges from the first step to every remaining step. The longest path is therefore the spine, and dependency_depth is 1, 2, 3 and 4 for S, M, L and XL.
independence_design.r3_finding_now_closed: R3 measured five semantic archetypes per required cell and ten scenario-name or cumulative-clause re-skins on top of them, and raised that as blocker B7. The corpus that measurement described has been discarded. No record of the re-minted corpus is a scenario rename, a numeric or seed substitution, or a clause-growth variant of any other record, in its own cell or in any other.
independence_design.how_the_new_axis_decides: each record is reduced to a recipe digest over the content tokens of task, instruction, question, signature and output contract, plus one clause digest per item, constraint and distractor, tagged with its section. Two records are siblings when their recipe digests are equal and one clause-digest set is contained in the other. A semantic group is a connected component of that relation, and containment rather than equality is what makes cumulative clause growth collapse.
independence_design.why_erasure_cannot_inflate_a_count: the axis erases synthetic identifiers, digit runs, stopwords, tokens shorter than three characters, and the corpus-wide union of every declared scenario slug. Erasing a token can only make two records look more alike, so it can only merge groups and never split them. A record whose declared scenario does not occur in its own rendered prompt is refused outright.
independence_design.residual_limitation: the group axis is lexical, not semantic. Two records that share a recipe but whose clause sets merely overlap without containment are counted as two groups, so an adversary willing to re-author clauses rather than append them can still buy a group. Closing that needs a model, not a digest. It is recorded here rather than papered over.

The commitment digest changed with the header rewording, and resolve refuses any bundle that does not quote the current commitment digest, so a stale bundle cannot be used by accident.

Its calibration split is used for screening, and its held-out split is burned because its worked answers were worker-visible in plaintext. No v2 held-out input may share a case id, payload digest, rendered prompt digest or normalised template with any v1 record.
